item.title: Iran's supreme leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the U.S. and Israel on Saturday against restarting the war amid weeks of heightened tensions and threats on both sides. He said there would be no geographical limitations for Iranian attacks if the war resumes.Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday no decision has been made yet on whether to restart military action against Iran, but "if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it and we have everything we need to be successful."President Trump said Friday the war with Iran is "going to end soon," without specifying how, as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to push for a peace deal being haggled over by Iran and the U.S.
New Updates
1m ago
U.S. blockade has redirected 144 ships in Strait of Hormuz, military says
The U.S. blockade on the Strait of Hormuz has now redirected 144 vessels, according to U.S. Central Command.
The U.S. had not provided an update on how many ships it had prevented from entering or exiting Iranian ports since exactly two weeks ago when it said it had redirected 138 vessels.
Earlier Saturday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had posted on X that the U.S. has taken out 1.5 billion barrels of oil without providing a timeframe.
Bessent posted that "transit levels are back to pre-conflict levels minus Iranian barrels." The U.S. has been guiding oil tankers out of the Persian Gulf under military escort over the past several months to do ship-to-ship oil transfers in the Gulf of Oman.
However, it's an expensive process and an open-ended mission at this point.

item.title: Pro-Palestinian protesters arrested outside U.S. Embassy in London
item.description:
Dozens of people were arrested at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy in London on Saturday in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action, police said.
London's Metropolitan Police said in a statement that 48 people had been arrested and the majority of the arrests were related to individuals expressing support for a proscribed organization.
"Officers remain at the scene and are continuing to make arrests," it said.
More than 100 people took part in the protest, with many holding signs reading: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."
Some protesters could be heard applauding and chanting "free, free Palestine" when people were taken away to police vans.
A protester holds a placard during a demonstration in support of Palestine Action, outside the U.S. Embassy, in London, Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026.
Alberto Pezzali/AP
The U.K. government outlawed the direct-action protest group last year as a terrorist organization. The ban makes membership in or support for Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison.
Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of Palestine Action outside the U.S. Consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland, holding placards akin to those in London. No arrests were reported there, but Police Scotland said inquiries to identify people seen wearing T-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organization were ongoing.
"Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate," it said.
The protests came before an appeal on Nov. 4 at the Supreme Court against Palestine Action's designation as a terror group. Supporters say the ban is draconian and it violates their freedom of speech.

item.title: French police clash with some protesters again as demonstrations continue
item.description:
French police fired tear gas and clashed with some protesters on Saturday as thousands marched across France again in largely peaceful demonstrations against soaring living costs and police violence.
Police said about 70,000 people demonstrated in Paris alone. France's interior ministry said about 320,000 people rallied nationwide.
Officers had made 27 arrests by 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, compared with 217 arrests a week ago. In the southern port city of Marseille, demonstrators clashed with police. In Lyon, France's third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene.
In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorized protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators, some of them in costume.
A protester waves a French flag while taking part in a demonstration in Lyon, France, on Oct. 31, 2026.
Jeff Pachoud /AFP via Getty Images
In Paris, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: "No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak" and "Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween." Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who has accused French President Emmanuel Macron's government of "taking an increasingly authoritarian turn," joined the march.
"We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students' demands, yes to giving citizens a voice," Camille Guerin, 31, said in the western city of Nantes.
In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest.

item.title: Residents evacuated from Russia-occupied city back in Ukraine
item.description:
Residents who were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as part of a U.S.-brokered temporary ceasefire crossed into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday.
The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump.
Oleshky is a city in Ukraine's southeastern Kherson region occupied by Russia since the first days of the Ukraine-Russia war. It is one of the most dire humanitarian crises of the conflict.
The ceasefire began at 3 a.m. Tuesday and is expected to continue through Sunday evening.
Residents evacuated from the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky during a humanitarian mission react upon arriving at an undisclosed location in Ukraine on Oct. 31, 2026.
Genya SAVILOV /AFP via Getty Images
The estimated 2,000 remaining residents of Oleshky were offered the choice of traveling to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.
Those who chose to return to Ukraine were taken to the Russian city of Anapa, then flown to Homel in Belarus, from where they proceeded back home.
Ukrainian authorities imposed restrictions on disclosing the number of evacuees or the border crossing location. The measures are to safeguard those who chose to remain in Oleshky as well as to protect future humanitarian missions, the organizers said.
Residents evacuated from the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky during a humanitarian mission disembark from a bus upon arriving at an undisclosed location in Ukraine on Oct. 31, 2026.
Genya SAVILOV /AFP via Getty Images

item.title: Family of real estate CEO wounded in Toronto home invasion, officials say
item.description:
A search is underway for three armed men who broke into a mansion in Toronto belonging to a real estate CEO in the early morning hours of Thursday and attacked and injured the family inside, authorities said.
The suspects, who were masked, forced their way through a back entrance of the five-bedroom home in the Bridle Path neighborhood at around 3:40 a.m. local time, wielding guns and a hammer, Toronto police said.
Once inside, police said they went to the second floor of the home and confronted 75-year-old David Morton; his wife, 64-year-old Doriana Morton; and their two adult daughters, Maggie and Cristina.
"There was a demand made for valuables from within the home," Toronto Police Service Inspector Kristy Smith told reporters. "Whether or not they escaped with anything is uncertain at this point."
On Saturday, Smith said one of the suspects they are looking for is 23-year-old Dejon Richards.
Richards is believed to have been accidentally shot in the shoulder by one of his accomplices during the incident, according to Smith. Richards went to the hospital, where he was interviewed by police, but they could not establish a connection to the incident and he was later discharged.
Police said David Morton, CEO of the MAC Group, and his daughters, ages 28 and 26, tried to fight off the intruders when shots were fired.
All three sustained gunshot wounds, Smith disclosed. And in a separate statement Friday, David Morton said that all four family members were also attacked by the suspects with the hammer.
David Morton said that he and his two daughters were still hospitalized Friday with gunshot wounds, but he did not provide details on their conditions.

item.title: Pope meets Villanova and Notre Dame basketball teams at the Vatican
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV met on Saturday with the basketball teams from Villanova and Notre Dame, along with thousands of U.S. fans in Italy, ahead of the two Catholic universities' season opener later this weekend.
About 7,000 people entered the Paul VI audience hall inside the Vatican on Saturday after a special private Mass in St. Peter's Basilica.
Leo, who is an avid tennis player and sports fan, said sports bring people together and can promote values such as fraternity, solidarity and peace.
"By acting as a concrete means of bringing people together, athletics can teach the values of cooperation and mutual sharing. This is increasingly necessary in an age marked by the distance that can be created by technology," he said, according to Vatican News.
Pope Leo XIV receives a basketball as a gift during an audience with delegations from Villanova University and the University of Notre Dame at the Paul VI Audience Hall in the Vatican on October 31, 2026.
Tiziana Fabi /AFP via Getty Images
The teams are in Rome for the U.S. college basketball season opener on Sunday — an event dubbed the Eternal City Tip-Off and created to honor the U.S.-born pope. The universities' men's and women's teams will play a doubleheader at the Palazzo Dello Sport, an 11,000-seat arena about a half-hour drive from the Vatican.
Leo, who is currently recovering from lung cancer surgery, graduated from Villanova in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science in mathematics.
"Growing up on the south side of Chicago, we oftentimes heard, 'Go Irish.' But as you all know, Prevost graduated from Villanova! So, the Pope doesn't take sides. Prevost has another opinion, but we won't do that now," Leo joked during the audience, according to Vatican News.

item.title: U.S. approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
item.description:
The State Department approved on Friday the sale of 500 Patriot missile defense systems to Ukraine at a cost $2.1 billion.
In a statement released Friday, the State Department said the purchase will be paid for by Ukraine with donations from Canada and European allies such as Germany and Norway, and that no U.S. funds are involved in the sale.
"This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe," the department said. It also added the principal contractor in this agreement is Lockheed Martin and that there would be "no adverse impact" on U.S. defense readiness.
Assembling Patriot missiles at Lockheed Martin's production facility in Camden, Arkansas.
CBS News
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy lauded the decision, and thanked President Trump, but warned that it may take years for the munitions to be delivered to Ukraine.
"We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger," Zelenskyy appealed on Friday evening.
In a post on X, the Ukrainian president said there had been more than 30 Russian strikes on his country's energy infrastructure in the past two weeks, targeting "the systems that sustain life in our cities and communities."
He appealed to the United States and European allies to provide Ukraine with the Patriot systems currently in their own stockpiles and replenish their arsenals with these 500 missiles, purchased by Ukraine, in the coming years.

item.title: How hard is it to recover the $6 billion stolen from Binance?
item.description:
After hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance, the cryptocurrency exchange said Friday it is working to recover the assets, a multi-pronged process that experts said involves coordinating with law enforcement and tracking the movement of the stolen funds.
"Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds," a Binance spokesperson said in a statement to CBS News.
Ari Redbord, a former federal prosecutor and the global head of policy at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence company tracking the stolen funds, called the heist the "largest bank robbery in human history."
TRM and other security firms attributed the attack to an elite hacking unit linked with North Korea known as "TraderTraitor." The funds were siphoned from internet-connected wallets on Binance's trading platform, Redbord said. The entire operation took roughly 20 minutes, according to Binance.
"The way a cryptocurrency exchange works is basically just like a bank. People put their funds in the bank, and those funds go onto wallets that are controlled by the exchange," Redbord told CBS News. "What North Korea was able to do was breach the hot wallets where Binance was keeping all of those funds."
As it works to recover the stolen assets, Binance vowed in a social media post to cover the full losses using company funds.
"We will pursue all available avenues to identify those responsible and hold them accountable," Binance said.
How does the recovery process work?
Redbord called the effort to recover Binance customers' funds the "fastest and largest" he's ever seen.
